summary: The transfer failures are caused by payment-service's expired outbound mTLS client certificate (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal, notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z) to bank-partner-api, not by the timeout config change, any deploy, a shared-component fault, or a partner-side outage (H1, confidence 0.70, medium). Onset is exact: bank_api_error_rate steps from ~0.2% to exactly 100.0% in the 12:15:00Z bucket, matches the cert notAfter, and was predicted 25 minutes in advance by a cert-watcher WARN, while payment_success_rate collapses from ~99% to ~2.5% with request_rate unchanged (~100 req/s). The HTTP error-rate panel is green because payment-service still returns 2xx and marks transfers PENDING_RETRY, hiding the total failure of the bank leg. All 35 buckets through 13:57Z remain pinned at 100% bank error with every logged handshake rejected and no new certificate appearing, indicating the cert expired and was never renewed. Alternatives are rejected by mechanism, timing and direct telemetry: no config/deploy change coincides with onset, cfg-2502 is a timeout key, and kafka/ledger-db telemetry is flat and normal.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Expired mTLS client certificate on payment-service → bank-partner-api
ranked_hypotheses.statement: payment-service's outbound mTLS client certificate (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal) expired at exactly 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z (notAfter). Every call to bank-partner-api is rejected at the TLS handshake ('remote error: tls: expired certificate, alert 45'), so transfers stop completing (payment_success_rate ~99% → ~2-3%) while payment-service still accepts requests and returns 2xx (marking transfers PENDING_RETRY), leaving the HTTP error-rate panel green. The fault origin is payment-service's credential lifecycle (no renewal automation / no rotation executed before or after expiry), not any deploy or config change.

causal_chain.claim: No cert rotation occurred; the client cert's notAfter silently reached 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z; a cert-watcher WARN at 11:50:26Z predicted it 25 min ahead
Cert expiry instantly breaks the mTLS handshake to bank-partner-api: 'remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45)'; every handshake logged is rejected, zero successes
All bank-partner-api calls fail → bank_api_error_rate jumps to exactly 100% at the 12:15Z bucket and stays pinned there
Transfers are marked PENDING_RETRY instead of returning errors → payment_success_rate collapses from ~99% to ~2-3% and never recovers
payment-service still returns HTTP 2xx to api-gateway, so HTTP error_rate stays flat ~0.1-0.32% with unchanged request_rate — the dashboard is green
Customers experience failed fund transfers; support raises ~40 tickets; onset (12:15Z) precedes the 12:32Z report

assumptions: The cert-watcher WARN and the 'expired certificate' error signature are accurate and causally tied (both VERIFIED observations, low risk).
bank-partner-api would accept a valid client cert (no concurrent partner-side outage) — cannot be confirmed because has_telemetry=false.

No renewal/rotation event exists in telemetry to explain the sustained 100% error rate; the absence of any recovery supports 'cert never renewed' rather than 'renewed but still failing', though a cert-rotation feed is not independently visible in the change records.

ranked_hypotheses.title: cfg-2502 timeout increase (3000→5000ms) stalls bank calls, causing silent transfer hangs
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The config change cfg-2502 on payment-service raised bank.api.timeout_ms from 3000 to 5000ms at 11:20Z 'after partner advisory', consistent with a degrading bank partner. Longer timeouts tie up payment-service workers on a stalled bank leg, so transfers hang/queue instead of failing fast; async completion collapses while HTTP responses remain 2xx — hence the green error-rate panel and the ~1h gap to the 12:15Z collapse.

causal_chain.claim: bank-partner-api began degrading; partner advisory prompts cfg-2502 raising bank.api.timeout_ms 3000→5000 at 11:20Z
Longer timeout holds payment-service workers on stalled bank calls, so transfers hang rather than fail
Transfer completion collapses while HTTP responses stay 2xx and error_rate stays flat
Customers report failed/hung transfers; dashboard green

assumptions: The partner was actually degrading before 11:20Z (no telemetry exists to confirm).
A timeout config could somehow produce a 100% error rate on the bank leg — not supported by any error signature.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Ruled out by mechanism and timing. The failure is total (100% bank_api_error_rate, pinned at exactly 100% through 13:57Z) with the specific signature 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)', which a timeout setting cannot produce (F7, F10, F12, F16, F25). Onset 12:15:00Z exactly equals the cert notAfter and was predicted by the cert-watcher 25 min in advance (F11, F15), whereas cfg-2502 predates onset by 54.5 min and no change occurred anywhere near 12:15Z (F14, F15). The change's key is a timeout, not a trust/credential setting (F16).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared-component neighbour fault (ledger-db or kafka) degrades payment transfers
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A neighbour writing to shared ledger-db (order/portfolio/settlement-service) or a kafka broker/consumer event degrades the shared resources payment-service depends on, so transfers silently fail downstream while payment-service's HTTP metrics stay healthy.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5510 (settlement-service v1.9.0, 10:30Z) or a shared-component event perturbs ledger-db/kafka
Shared ledger-db/kafka contention degrades payment-service's downstream transfer completion
Transfer success collapses; HTTP error_rate flat; customers report failures

assumptions: Any shared-component degradation exists at all — no ledger-db/kafka logs were retrieved and no config change there was found.
dep-5510 touching settlement-service (off the transfer path) could propagate to payment-service.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: No evidence of any ledger-db or kafka anomaly: the sole failure signature in the window is the bank mTLS path (F12 'no other error class... 4xx/DB/queue'); kafka under_replicated_partitions flat at 0.0 (F20), kafka messages_in_per_s steady (F21), ledger-db connections_active flat ~60-63 (F23), ledger-db slow_queries_per_min bump precedes onset and returns to baseline by 12:10Z (F24). dep-5510 touches settlement-service, off the transfer path (F16). Onset aligns with a cert expiry, not with any shared-component event (F15).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Concurrent bank-partner-api (external acquirer) outage
ranked_hypotheses.statement: bank-partner-api itself is degraded or down (external dependency failure), so transfers accepted by payment-service never complete on the partner leg, producing failures invisible to payment-service's HTTP error panel — the HIST-105 shape ('Payment failures: bank partner API outage').

causal_chain.claim: payment-service's on-path calls to the partner fail asynchronously after returning 2xx
transfer success collapses; customers report failures; dashboard green

assumptions: A partner-side fault would coincidentally start at exactly 12:15:00Z, the same instant payment-service's client cert expired.
The partner leg is unobservable (has_telemetry=false), so a concurrent partner condition can never be positively excluded.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The observed error is a client-side TLS handshake rejection caused by payment-service's own expired client certificate (F10, F11, F12, F29) — a fault on the client leg, not a partner-side service failure. The exact-second alignment of onset with cert notAfter (F15) and the closer precedent HIST-106 (credential_expiry) over HIST-105 rule this out as the origin. A concurrent partner fault cannot be formally excluded (no telemetry) but is not required to explain any evidence.

facts.statement: payment-service's outbound mTLS client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal failed with 'remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' and notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z; the earliest failure log (12:15:27Z) marks a payment PENDING_RETRY due to rejected mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api.

A cert-watcher WARN at 11:50:26Z predicted the expiry 25 minutes ahead ('expires in 25 minutes, notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z'), matching onset exactly; the dominant log patterns are 171 expired-cert errors and 140 PENDING_RETRY entries.
payment-service bank_api_error_rate jumps from ~0.2% to exactly 100.0% starting in the 12:15:00Z bucket and remains pinned at 100% through 13:57Z (35 buckets, min=max=mean=100.0, no missing points).
payment_success_rate collapses from ~99% before 12:15Z to ~2.5% at the 12:15:00Z bucket and never recovers, staying in the ~1.98-3.06% band across all 35 buckets through 13:57Z.

payment-service HTTP error_rate stays flat/normal (~0.1-0.32%) across the whole window and request_rate is unchanged (~97-105 req/s), so the ~97% completion collapse is a per-request failure of the bank path, not reduced traffic, and the HTTP panel is misleading.

No new certificate appears in payment-service logs from 13:00Z onward: a contains='cert' search over 13:00Z-13:59Z matches only the expired-cert pattern (91 ERRORs, original CN/notAfter values, no renewal event), and every logged handshake (86 matches) is rejected with zero successful handshakes.
The expired-cert error continues unbroken to the last log at 13:58:39Z, with no cessation in the 13:40Z-13:59Z window (57 ERROR vs 3 benign INFO).

Exactly one config change exists in the 10:00Z-14:30Z window across all services: cfg-2502 on payment-service, bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 at 11:20:00Z; and no config or flag change exists at or near onset (count=0 in 12:00Z-13:00Z and 11:30Z-14:00Z).

No deployment exists on the transfer path in the incident day: per-service queries return count=0 for payment-service, api-gateway, and bank-partner-api, and the all-services deployment query over the 12:00Z-13:00Z onset hour returns count=0.

The deployment query backend is serving data: the same query type over the known-populated 10:00Z-11:00Z window returns exactly one deployment, dep-5510 (settlement-service v1.9.0 at 10:30:00Z), so the empty onset-window results are trustworthy negatives.

The nearest changes are not coincident with onset: dep-5510 is 105 minutes before onset and touches settlement-service, which is off the api-gateway -> payment-service -> {ledger-db, bank-partner-api, kafka} transfer path; cfg-2502 is 54.5 minutes before onset and its key is a timeout, not a credential/trust setting.

kafka shows no degradation during the incident: under_replicated_partitions is flat 0.0 (150/150 points) and messages_in_per_s is steady (mean 2530.73, 150/150 points) with no throughput drop when payment failures began.

ledger-db shows no anomaly coincident with onset: connections_active is flat ~60-63 (150/150 points) and slow_queries_per_min's only bump (max 9.63) precedes onset and has returned to baseline by the 12:10Z bucket.

Historical precedent HIST-106 (2025-06-30) 'Settlement mTLS certificate expired' has symptoms 'tls handshake failures','expired certificate', category 'credential_expiry', root_cause 'Client certificate expired; no renewal automation' - matching the current signature far more closely than HIST-105 (bank partner returned 5xx).
The transfer call path is api-gateway -> payment-service -> {ledger-db, bank-partner-api, kafka}; ledger-db and kafka are shared components, and bank-partner-api is external with has_telemetry=false.

assumptions: The cert-watcher WARN and the 'expired certificate' error signature are accurate and causally tied (both VERIFIED observations, low risk).
bank-partner-api would accept a valid client certificate (no concurrent partner-side outage) - this cannot be confirmed because the partner has no telemetry available.

No renewal/rotation event exists in telemetry to explain the sustained 100% error rate; the absence of any recovery supports 'cert never renewed' rather than 'renewed but still failing', though a cert-rotation feed is not independently visible in the change records.
The deployment backend's empty results for the onset window reflect genuinely no deploys, validated against a known-populated control window, rather than a transient blind backend.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) payment-service errors are bank-side only: total_matched=314 with ERROR=311 vs WARN=3; no other error class (4xx/DB/queue) appears in the top patterns.

timeline.event: dep-5510 deployed: settlement-service v1.9.0 (off the transfer path), the only deployment in 10:00Z-14:00Z; 105 minutes before onset.
Config change cfg-2502 on payment-service: bank.api.timeout_ms raised 3000->5000ms 'after partner advisory' - the only config change in the window, 54.5 minutes before onset.
Cert-watcher WARN: client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expires in 25 minutes (notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z).
Certificate notAfter reached. bank_api_error_rate steps from ~0.2% to exactly 100% and payment_success_rate collapses from ~99% to ~2.5%; failure state persists through 13:57Z.

Earliest failure log: payment 45f233b6 marked PENDING_RETRY, 'mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected' with 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' and CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z.
Incident INC-005 reported by support lead: ~40 tickets about failed fund transfers; payment-service HTTP error-rate panel shows nothing unusual.
From 13:00Z onward, no new certificate appears in payment-service logs; all 86 logged handshakes are rejected with the original expired CN/notAfter values.
Last log still 'bank-partner-api call failed: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45)'; error tunnel unbroken to end of telemetry, no renewal and no recovery.

recommended_actions.action: Immediate mitigation: issue and deploy a renewed client certificate for CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal on payment-service's outbound mTLS to bank-partner-api, then restart/reload the payment-service TLS context and confirm bank_api_error_rate returns from 100% toward the ~0.2% baseline and payment_success_rate recovers to ~99%.
recommended_actions.rationale: The failure signature is 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' on our own client cert with notAfter=12:15:00Z, onset matches the expiry instant exactly, and 100% bank error with zero successful handshakes persists to the last log; a valid cert is the direct fix and the recovery check discriminates H1 from a concurrent partner-side condition.

recommended_actions.action: Immediate (operational): drain/replay the PENDING_RETRY transfers queued since 12:15Z once the bank leg is restored, and give support a holding statement that the payment-service HTTP error panel is misleading during the outage.
recommended_actions.rationale: Transfers were accepted as 2xx and marked PENDING_RETRY rather than failed, so a backlog of incomplete transfers exists while customers see failures; the green HTTP panel is why the issue reached support tickets instead of alerting.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT roll back cfg-2502 and do not revert dep-5510; leave both in place pending verification.
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-2502 is a timeout key (bank.api.timeout_ms) that cannot expire a credential and predates onset by 54.5 min; dep-5510 touches settlement-service off the transfer path 105 min before onset. Neither is the cause, and a rollback adds risk without addressing the mechanism.

recommended_actions.action: Short term: after the renewed cert is in place, verify the fix by confirming payment_success_rate returns to ~99% and bank_api_error_rate falls to baseline across several consecutive buckets, and confirm successful handshake log lines appear (as HIST-106's remediation pattern).
recommended_actions.rationale: The error state was pinned at 100% with no recovery for the entire 12:15Z-13:57Z span, so recovery must be positively observed rather than assumed; HIST-106 shows 'issued new cert' as the resolution.

recommended_actions.action: Short term: add an alert/action on the existing cert-watcher WARN so certificate expiries page before notAfter (the watcher fired 25 minutes ahead), and confirm the renewal actually executes rather than only warning.
recommended_actions.rationale: The cert-watcher gave 25 minutes of lead time that was not actioned, and no renewal appeared in logs after 12:15Z, indicating the warning path is not wired to automated or on-call action.

recommended_actions.action: Long term: implement automated client-certificate renewal/rotation for payment-service's bank-partner-api mTLS (and audit all service-to-external mTLS certs for the same gap), with rotation recorded in the change feed so credential-lifecycle events are auditable.
recommended_actions.rationale: HIST-106's root cause was 'client certificate expired; no renewal automation' with 'added expiry alert' as resolution; the current incident shows no cert-rotation entry in the deployment or config feeds, so this class of failure will recur without automation.

recommended_actions.action: Long term: make silent async/bank-leg failures visible on dashboards - e.g., alert on payment_success_rate / bank_api_error_rate / PENDING_RETRY backlog rather than only HTTP error_rate - so a green HTTP panel cannot mask total transfer failure.
recommended_actions.rationale: For ~1.5 hours transfers failed at ~97% while HTTP error_rate stayed ~0.1-0.32% and request_rate was unchanged, so the panel in use gave no signal; HIST-109 shows the same invisibility pattern.

data_gaps: bank-partner-api has has_telemetry=false, so there is no partner-side log or metric to check whether the partner changed its cert/trust config concurrently; a simultaneous partner-side condition cannot be formally excluded.

No deployment or config record exposes certificate or secret rotation events; the absence of a cert-rotation entry supports 'never renewed' but the cert-changed event itself is not independently visible in the change timeline.
No cert-watcher or renewal-service log was queried for 13:00Z-13:59Z, so it is unconfirmed whether a renewal job ran and failed versus never ran at all after 12:15Z.

latency_p99_ms and bank_api_request_rate for payment-service timed out, so it could not be confirmed whether tail latency rose or how many raw outbound bank calls occurred (service-wide request_rate was used as a proxy).

kafka and ledger-db WARN-level logs were never retrieved (budget exhausted); only their metric health is established, so log-level errors on those components cannot be ruled out, though their queried metrics were flat/normal.
No deployment query explicitly covered 13:00Z-13:59Z, and the bank-partner-api query over the tight 11:30Z-14:30Z window timed out (answered only over the wider 04-01 to 04-02 span with count=0).
settlement-service was checked only at WARN level (3 benign entries); its ERROR-level logs and key metrics were not retrieved.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: A new/rotated certificate appearing in payment-service logs with the error rate remaining at 100% after the rotation took effect - this would mean H1's mechanism is incomplete or a concurrent partner-side condition exists.
Evidence that bank-partner-api was itself rejecting valid client certificates or was failing at ~12:15Z (e.g., partner-side telemetry or an announced partner change), which would support H3 over H1.
A deploy or config/flag change on payment-service, bank-partner-api, or a shared transfer-path component within minutes of 12:15:00Z, which would reopen H2 or a change-origin cause.
kafka or ledger-db telemetry or logs showing an anomaly coincident with 12:15Z (e.g., partition reassignment, connection saturation, error logs), which would reopen H4.
A successful mTLS handshake logged to bank-partner-api while payment_success_rate remains ~2% - which would show the bank leg is not the failure point and redirect the investigation.

findings.statement: payment-service dependency map: outbound edges to ledger-db (kind=db), bank-partner-api (kind=external, has_telemetry=false), kafka (kind=queue-produce); inbound edge from api-gateway (kind=http). So the transfer call path is api-gateway -> payment-service -> {ledger-db, bank-partner-api, kafka}.

ledger-db and kafka are shared components (shared=true): ledger-db is written by four independent services — order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service, settlement-service — so a neighbour can degrade payment-service via that shared database. bank-partner-api has no telemetry at all.

Exactly one config change in the wider window 10:00Z–14:30Z (all services): cfg-2502 on payment-service, key bank.api.timeout_ms, old_value 3000 -> new_value 5000, changed_at 2026-04-02T11:20:00Z by p.nair, 'Raise bank API timeout after partner advisory'. This sits directly on the transfer path (payment-service -> bank-partner-api) and predates the 12:32Z report.

So no rollback-able deploy is visible on the transfer path in this window.

Historical precedents (leads only): HIST-105 (2025-11-19) 'Payment failures: bank partner API outage' with symptoms 'payment failures','bank api errors', category dependency_failure, resolution 'Waited for partner; queued retries' — same symptom shape as this incident. Two async/queue-shaped precedents exist: HIST-104 'notification-service lag after Kafka broker rebalance' and HIST-112 'Settlement consumer stalled after partition reassignment' (both kafka consumer-lag symptoms), and HIST-109 'Token validation regression after auth library upgrade' which shows a service-level failure can be invisible on a naive error-rate panel.

Inference: the transfer path has two failure modes that would NOT surface on payment-service's own HTTP error_rate — (a) the bank-partner-api call, which has has_telemetry=false so no server-side telemetry corroborates or refutes the partner's health, and (b) the kafka queue-produce edge, i.e. async post-transfer processing. The only timed change on the path (cfg-2502, timeout 3000->5000ms at 11:20Z) lengthens how long a stalled bank call ties up payment-service workers rather than shortening failures, so it is a candidate contributor to silent/hanging transfers, not to HTTP 5xx. Cause is not established by dependency data alone.

findings.statement: Most likely fault location: the expired client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal on payment-service's outbound mTLS to bank-partner-api — NOT any deploy or config change. Discriminating evidence: (1) onset 12:15:00Z equals cert notAfter exactly, and a cert-watcher WARN at 11:50:26Z predicted it 25 min ahead, whereas the last change predates onset by 54.5 min; (2) no change within minutes of onset anywhere (config count=0 in 11:30Z-14:00Z); (3) the only on-path change (cfg-2502) is a timeout value that cannot expire a credential; (4) the sole failure signature is 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' with 311 ERRORs on the bank path only.

kafka exposes no consumer_lag metric; its available_metrics are exactly ['cpu_pct','messages_in_per_s','under_replicated_partitions'] (call for consumer_lag returned not_found). So the classic consumer-lag symptom cannot be measured on this kafka id.
kafka under_replicated_partitions is flat 0.0 across the entire 11:30Z–13:59Z window (min/max/mean all 0.0, 150/150 points, no missing data) — no broker/partition degradation on the shared queue.

kafka messages_in_per_s is steady across the window (mean 2530.73, min 2316.83, max 2784.18, first 2607.8, last 2554.26, 150/150 points) — no throughput drop or backlog spike when payment failures began at ~12:15Z.
ledger-db exposes no connection_pool_usage metric; available_metrics are ['connections_active','cpu_pct','disk_used_pct','replication_lag_ms','slow_queries_per_min'].

ledger-db connections_active is flat ~60-63 across the whole window (summary min 55.32, max 69.24, mean 62.01, 150/150 points) — no connection-pool saturation on the shared database during the incident.

ledger-db slow_queries_per_min is near baseline (mean 1.48) with its only bump at 11:50Z–12:00Z (avg 2.63 then 6.6, max 9.63) which PRECEDES the 12:15Z payment onset and has fully returned to ~1.0 by the 12:10Z bucket — so ledger-db shows no independent anomaly coincident with the failure onset.

bank_api_error_rate at 180s granularity from 12:15Z through 13:57Z is pinned at exactly 100.0% for every bucket (min=100, max=100, mean=100.0, last=100, 35 points, missing_points=0) — there is no fallback toward ~0.2% at any point; the 100% state that began at the 12:15:00Z bucket persists through the latest data.

findings.statement: Re-run of the all-services deployment query over the onset window 2026-04-02T12:00:00Z-13:00:00Z returns count=0 with scope 'all services' (attempts=2, partial=false, no warnings) — no deployment or rollback anywhere in the hour containing the 12:15Z onset. Note this window ends at 13:00Z, so it does not by itself cover 13:00-13:59Z (covered separately: tc-026 timed out; no deployments surfaced in any other query).

Backend validation: the SAME query type over the known-populated window 10:00Z-11:00Z returns exactly one deployment, dep-5510 (settlement-service v1.9.0, deployed_at 2026-04-02T10:30:00Z, author ci-bot, summary 'Batch settlement report export', status 'live', rolled_back_at null). So the deployment API is serving data and the empty 12:00Z-13:00Z / 11:30Z-13:59Z results are trustworthy negatives, not a blind backend.

No deployment or rollback exists on any transfer-path component in the incident day: per-service queries over 2026-04-02T00:00Z-13:59Z return count=0 for payment-service (scope 'payment-service', attempts=2), count=0 for api-gateway, and count=0 for bank-partner-api. The payment-service query is the second independent confirmation of the empty result (after tc-008/tc-024), and bank-partner-api has no deployable change history at all.

Config/flag changes are likewise absent at onset: the all-services config-change query over 2026-04-02T12:00:00Z-13:00:00Z returns count=0. Combined with F14 (count=0 in 11:30Z-14:00Z), there is no config or flag change on payment-service, bank-partner-api or any shared transfer-path component within ~40 minutes before or after the 12:15Z onset.
